findings.evidence: `rg` hits: code lines 205 and 208 are `FlatOfOrder γ t₀ 1` and `FlatOfOrderBasepoint γ a b 1`; `ConditionB` lines 254-259 require only `SectorCompatible`; roadmap `Suggested.lean` lines 102-104 and README lines 182-185 say A′ includes a prescribed pole order.
findings.fix: Give A′ access to the prescribed pole order, e.g. by parameterizing it by `f`/`meromorphicOrderAt` or by replacing `S : Finset ℂ` with ordered singularity data; otherwise do not label this predicate as HW condition (A′) for the general theorem.
findings.issue: `ConditionAprime` hard-codes `FlatOfOrder ... 1` for both interior crossings and the basepoint, so a pole of order `n > 1` can satisfy A′ with only first-order flatness; `ConditionB` only imposes `SectorCompatible` and does not recover the missing flatness order.

findings.evidence: Code lines 182-183 and 192-193 use `‖γ t - (γ t₀ + (t - t₀) • t_plus)‖` / endpoint analogues; the author reply confirms HW uses the tangent line projection and that the current definition diverges for `n ≥ 2`.
findings.fix: Define higher-order flatness using distance to the one-sided tangent affine line, equivalently orthogonal projection onto that line, and apply the same correction to the basepoint version.
findings.issue: `FlatOfOrder` and `FlatOfOrderBasepoint` measure deviation from the parametrized affine point `γ t₀ + (t - t₀) • v`, not distance to the tangent line/projection used in HW Def. 3.2; a curve lying on its tangent line with nonlinear speed is geometrically flat of all orders but can fail this predicate for `n ≥ 2`.

summary: ConditionAprime is still weaker than HW condition (A′) for higher-order poles, and the exported general flatness predicate does not match the cited geometric definition. The author reply identifies a roadmap-signature gap, but this PR still exports the weakened predicate as the paper-faithful HW condition.
